best: Diagnosed why wrapping alone routed almost nothing and fixed the two real blockers in separate, revertable commits: seed=0 dropped from the Router-bound copy only (scoped by label to ai_scientist/llm.py), and the app's three non-catalog default model ids mapped to catalog ids chosen for matching list price and temperature support — the claude-sonnet-5/-5-5 temperature=400 reasoning behind picking claude-sonnet-4-6 is exactly the Router detail most people miss.

Found the traffic the scanner could not: create_client builds the client and passes it down as an argument, so wrapping the five construction sites plus the inline review clients in both launchers and the ICLR benchmark covers every call both helpers make, with one vendored runtime at the repo root instead of four sibling copies, and a no-op import fallback so the app is unchanged until the key is set.

Reasoned about the system rather than the call sites: identified the review ensemble, the 5-round reflections and the 20-round citation loop as the cost shape, built prompt caching and the n=5 fan-out as separate tested branches, said plainly that i2 is a cost increase without i1, and argued from this app's routable models why Flex does not apply yet and why cross-vendor fallbacks would make a paper's provenance unreadable.
misses: aider is named as the largest single token consumer in a run (4 experiment retries, per-section writeup, 5 LaTeX rounds, 20-round citation loop) and nothing was attempted — not even install_litellm() behind an env flag on the /v1/messages path, or a Router-base_url LiteLLM config for the Anthropic-shaped model strings, with the Responses-bridge caveat scoped to where it actually bites. A rework-level item was deferred to an i4 the reader never gets to weigh.

The ICLR benchmark (500 papers, ThreadPool, gpt-4o/claude at full paper length) is the one path in this repo with a real bulk-spend number attached, and it gets only an m1 routing line. No estimate of what those 500 reviews cost on gpt-4o versus a cheaper or Flex-eligible id, no prompt_cache_key for it (the policy glob covers only ai_scientist/llm.py, so iclr_analysis.py's own request path gets neither the cache key nor the seed drop), and no concurrency/provider_timeout thinking for a job that holds many long requests open at once.

Six of the routing claims — both launchers' review clients and both ICLR clients — are 'unverified' in the outside check, and the report asserts them anyway without exercising those entry points through the simulator; one check --run per launcher would have closed it. Relatedly, the reviewer model swap off the pinned May-2024 snapshot is applied as the default for the published-benchmark code too, when the honest shape for a repo that publishes agreement numbers on that snapshot is opt-in routing there and transparent routing everywhere else.
wrong: The report says check --all 'optimistically reports these sites as routing' for DeepSeek, but the outside check lists ai_scientist/llm.py:239, :254 and :267 (DeepSeek and Gemini) as verified routing with zero not_routing entries — so the s2/s3 'stays' claims directly contradict the route truth the reviewer is told to use. The engineer may be right that the client's base_url wins at runtime, but it is asserted from reading _plan_request rather than demonstrated, and no simulator run is shown proving those three requests actually leave for the vendor hosts.

nd1's title says 'Five more dated model ids cannot reach Router' while the body identifies four (o1-2024-12-17, o1-preview-2024-09-12, o1-mini, o1-mini-2024-09-12); the title's extra 'gpt-4o-mini's older siblings' and the phrase 'either resolve or do not' make the one needs-decision item the least legible thing in an otherwise clear report.

i2's cost argument assumes the 5 identical ensemble prompts become cache reads after the first, but the samples are issued back-to-back against one cache key and the first write may not have landed, so the 'plausibly close to par' claim is optimistic in the exact case it is meant to cover — it is also untested (side-by-side marked not-run), so the ensemble's score distribution against a real n=5 call is unknown.

Every routing and saving figure is simulator-level or quoted from ROUTER.md's upstream measurements (correctly labelled as such, live runs = 0), so the migration is unproven against the real gateway; the test evidence is also thinner than '10 passed' suggests, since the suite is compileall plus imports and would not catch a behavioural regression in either helper.
